fields.explanation: setV(10) asks React to re-render Counter with the new value; it does not change the v variable in the current closure, so console.log(v) prints the value from this render, 0. On the next click v is 10, because Counter has run again and useState returned the updated state. Updating state inside an event handler is normal and never throws; an unconditional setter call in the component body is what loops and throws.
